As a disclaimer I don't have any experience homesteading, but am in a similar boat in that I am interested in eventually having one, though realistically not for a few years. I've found YouTube to be a great source, though it can be hit or miss in some ways. I've come across a few channels where I get the feeling that they are less about homesteading than about "YouTube homesteading" and don't really give a realistic impression of what life is like. Kind of like a homesteader click bait where they are more interested in generating views by romanticizing the lifestyle than actually giving people sound advice. I am partial to watching dirtpatchheaven and jnull0, though they may not be your cup of tea. I get the feeling that they are a little more on the practical side.

You mentioned that you have some experience and have done some research. It might be nice to start organizing now, making a list of the things that you will need, pricing them out and setting some money aside. I think that budgeting is going to play a really big role in making your homestead sustainable for you, and your start up costs are going to be fairly significant. When you get closer to your buy-in you might also consider putting the word out to your family to lookout for certain things, they may be able to help you pick up some quality second hand equipment or give a tip-off on a good piece of land that might not be listed for sale.

I would also recommend taking a look around for some videos on "The downside of homesteading", "things no one tells you about homesteading", "Things I wish someone had told me about homesteading", "homesteading nightmare" or "homesteading mistakes", not to discourage you from doing it, but because I remember seeing a few videos that bring up some of the particular challenges that are rarely mentioned. It is a good to take a look at the things that have gone really wrong for people so you can avoid their mistakes. It might also help to gain a more realistic picture, since we most often hear from successful people and not the ones that failed and gave up.

As other posters have said, it is a good idea to start practicing as much as you can right now. Little things like gardening or container growing, canning etc.

Good luck in your search.
